public_rationale: Under the reading that this describes the AI investment boom, the absolute denial is contradicted. Meta reports measurable business improvements and explicitly says experienced benefits encourage continued heavy investment. That establishes a documented contribution from returns; it does not establish that the industry's total spending is justified.
limitations: The causal evidence is management testimony.
If 'bubble' means only unjustified speculative excess, these records do not isolate that component.
Advertising improvements do not establish positive net returns on all generative AI investment.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The AI bubble is not the result of any actual return on investment, whether revenue, profitability, productivity gains, or anything tangible or measurable.

statement.excerpt: The AI bubble isn’t a result of any actual return on investment — whether that be in purely monetary terms, like revenue or profitability , productivity gains, or anything tangible or measurable.

from_speaker: isn’t a result of any actual return on investment
our_interpretation: Read 'AI bubble' as the AI investment boom discussed in the surrounding text, through July 15, 2026.
Read 'any' as denying that demonstrated business benefits contributed to that investment. This is stronger than saying that returns do not justify the total investment.
A productivity gain alone does not establish what caused investment. Evidence must also connect demonstrated benefits to investment decisions.
criteria.support_condition: Credible evidence establishes that demonstrated business benefits made no contribution to the investment boom.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Documented investment decisions identify demonstrated AI benefits as a reason for continued substantial investment.
